subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class owner-confirmed lifecycle for promoting assistant, skill, and tool outputs into durable memory or reusable evidence?
rationale: The source shows adjacent approval and provenance primitives, but choosing whether this becomes a core lifecycle, a memory-plugin contract, or an external ClawHub/SCBKR-style integration is product and security policy, not a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Sponsor a design RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the minimal lifecycle states, owner confirmation semantics, revocation model, plugin/memory API boundary, and upgrade path before implementation.

options.title: Scope to plugin APIs first
options.body: Treat the immediate core work as exposing the missing generic hooks/metadata so memory or governance plugins can enforce owner confirmation without baking a full policy into core.

options.title: Route outside core
options.body: Decline first-class OpenClaw support and ask SCBKR, UMP, or ClawHub packages to own the workflow if current extension points are considered sufficient.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a design RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the minimal lifecycle states, owner confirmation semantics, revocation model, plugin/memory API boundary, and upgrade path before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Skill Workshop and security-boundary history makes steipete the best available routing owner for the product-shape decision.
